intro: Apollo 15 landed in Hadley Rille / Apennine Mountains on July 30, 1971 — the first "J-class" mission with extended surface stay, Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV), and a scientist-trained pilot (David Scott). Scott and Irwin drove 28 km total across three EVAs, found the Genesis Rock (~4.1 Ga anorthosite, primary crust), and on live TV dropped a feather + hammer to demonstrate Galileo's gravity test.

images.caption: Apollo 15 crew + the Lunar Roving Vehicle in pre-mission training — Scott + Irwin would drive the first wheels on the Moon.
Jim Irwin saluting beside the LRV with Mt Hadley Delta behind — the first images of the Apennine Mountains from the surface.
David Scott at the rim of Hadley Rille — first time astronauts stood at the edge of an ancient lava channel on another world.
Hadley Plain panorama — Falcon descent stage + LRV + Mt Hadley Delta on the horizon.
Sample 15415 "Genesis Rock" — pure ferroan anorthosite, ~4.1 billion years old. A fragment of the Moon's primary magma-ocean crust.
